articles.title: Fractal Candy Chaos

articles.what: Three-octave fractal noise mixing candy transparency zones — chaotic depth variation Up close: Hot pink-coral surface with fine, noisy wriggling contour grain, 3-8 px, and scattered clumps of royal blue and purple, 20-60 px, where the pink thins out. Edges are crinkly like fractal noise or topographic lines; no sharp shapes, no sparkle. From a distance: Reads as a pink bubblegum surface with blue-violet blotches; about 80 percent pink, the blue clumps scatter like bruises. Measured spec (average): metal 252, roughness 55, coat 249. Shine: gloss. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, hood.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Fractal Candy Chaos" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: broad panels show the blue clumps
Small trim gets mostly pink
White or black numbers read well on the pink; blue clumps can nick thin strokes; bold digits are best.
Fine stripes or dots at low strength: calm base so graphics show cleanly
Pairs well with: white, chrome, black, lime.
pitfalls: Not a smooth solid candy pink: the blue-purple mottling is clearly visible
Not a transparent candy depth effect in the render: the pink looks flat
Avoid: small numbers over chaos, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 252 (chrome or mirror tier), roughness 55 (high gloss), clearcoat 249 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over chaos, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine stripes or dots at low strength: calm base so graphics show cleanly; outlined graphics or numbers plates: sit cleanly on the pink
Patterns to avoid: camo, marble or other mottle patterns: same noisy language, mud

Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Crystal Lattice
articles.summary: Grey faceted crystal grains with bright cleavage edges and pin-point glints. Reads as a cool slate blue-grey faceted metal; facets stay visible as a shimmering light-dark mosaic, with a pale sparkle on the lightest ones.
articles.what: A grown mineral bed — faceted crystal grains with bright cleavage edges and pin-point glints. Materials & Physics finish. Up close: Irregular polygon facets, about 20-60px, each a flat ramp from dark slate to pale periwinkle in its own random direction, like crushed quartz or cut glass. Thin bright cleavage edges sit between facets, with a few tiny white pin-point glints; colour stays cool blue-grey. From a distance: Reads as a cool slate blue-grey faceted metal; facets stay visible as a shimmering light-dark mosaic, with a pale sparkle on the lightest ones. Measured spec (average): metal 178, roughness 125, coat 24. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.

articles.summary: Grey steel with flowing wavy light-and-dark bands, like ripples in water or folded metal. A mid-grey satin steel with a flowing zebra-grain movement; at distance a soft mottled grey with a wavy vertical direction.

articles.title: Ferrofluid Spikes
articles.summary: Dark near-black surface with a regular lattice of small round highlighted mounds; semi-matte, high metal, faint sparkle. A black car with a faint polka-dot or studded-rubber grain; dots blur to a dark grey haze, so it reads as dark metallic black with a subtle dotted sheen.
articles.what: Ferrofluid under a magnet — the Rosensweig spike lattice, black iron mounds with glossy steel caps. Materials & Physics finish. Dots vary from dim to bright across the tile, nothing between them.
